study_identification_part.si_4_title: Delineating the Heterogeneity of Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Normative Models of Dynamic Brain Functional Networks

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study uses three datasets: (1) Cam-CAN (Cambridge Centre for Aging and Neuroscience) as Dataset 1 with 644 healthy individuals for building the normative model; (2) MCAD (Multicenter Alzheimer Disease Imaging Consortium) as Dataset 2 with 257 NC, 257 MCI, and 295 AD patients from 7 sites; (3) ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) as Dataset 3 with 259 NC and 184 MCI patients for longitudinal validation.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scans of 1896 individuals were acquired from 3 datasets. Dataset 1, which included 644 healthy individuals, was used in this work to build a normative model and was obtained from the Cambridge Centre for Aging and Neuroscience repository (Cam-CAN)... Dataset 2 comprised 257 normal control (NC) participants, 257 patients with MCI, and 295 patients with AD from the MCAD (Multicenter Alzheimer Disease Imaging Consortium) dataset. Dataset 3 included 259 NC participants and 184 patients with MCI from the ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) database..."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Huo2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Participants, L46-47

answer.MCAD: deviation estimation and subtype identification for AD and MCI

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Dataset 1 (Cam-CAN) was exclusively used to train the normative model with Gaussian process regression. Dataset 2 (MCAD) was used to estimate deviation patterns and identify AD and MCI subtypes using clustering. Dataset 3 (ADNI) was used as an independent validation dataset to investigate the robustness of findings and longitudinal changes in MCI subtypes, including Kaplan-Meier survival analysis for MCI-to-AD conversion.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Dataset 1, which included 644 healthy individuals, was used in this work to build a normative model... Dataset 3 included 259 NC participants and 184 patients with MCI from the ADNI database, which was used to investigate longitudinal changes in MCI." "We replicated the experiment on dataset 3 to investigate the robustness of our findings. We used Kaplan-Meier survival analysis to assess the risk of MCI subtypes progressing to AD."

model-1.model-name: sex-specific normative age model of dynamic functional connectivity features

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using the entire Cam-CAN dataset (Dataset 1) with 644 healthy control participants. The study used 10-fold cross-validation to assess generalizability before applying the model, but the final normative model was trained based on the full Dataset 1. The 34 features (17 a-FCS and 17 f-FCS) were each modeled using Gaussian process regression with sex and age as covariates.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We estimated normative models to predict each dFC feature using sex and age as covariates in Gaussian process regression in a large healthy reference cohort from dataset 1." "To assess the generalizability of the model, we used 10-fold cross-validation before applying the model trained on datasets 1 to dataset 2 and dataset 3. Finally, the normative model was trained based on dataset 1 for subsequent disease deviation analyses."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Huo2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling for a-FCS and f-FCS, L60-61

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The normative model was built using the entire Cam-CAN dataset (n=644) with mean age 54.8 years and SD 18.5 years. Since the entire dataset was used for training the final model (with 10-fold cross-validation only for generalizability assessment), the overall-phase and train-phase statistics are identical. The original Cam-CAN dataset includes participants across the adult lifespan, but specific min/max/median values are not reported in this paper.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The normative model was built using the entire Cam-CAN dataset (n=644) with 327 females (50.8%) and 317 males (49.2%). The sex distribution is well-balanced. Since the entire dataset was used for training the final model, the overall-phase and train-phase statistics are identical. The study mentions building sex-specific normative age models.
